turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hi, how are things with you?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm good, thanks.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should I bring cash to Japan or just use my card?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Bring some cash. Cards are widely accepted in cities now, but smaller restaurants, temples and rural places often still want cash.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How much?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Enough for a couple of days is a good start. Convenience store cash machines usually accept foreign cards, so you can top up.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can I ask about something else? My closet is overflowing. I can't find anything in there.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A good sort will help. For the stuff you don't wear anymore, do you want to donate it, sell it online, or just store it in boxes for now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh, quick word with my aunt. Tell you when I'm done.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Omar, stop eating the croutons, they're for the salad.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: I'm quality checking.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: You've quality checked half the tray.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: They're really good though. What did you put on them?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Garlic, olive oil, a bit of parmesan. Can you pass me the lettuce from the fridge?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Which one, the round one or the long one?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The long one. And wash your hands, you're all oily.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What was the name of that show we watched?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: I can't remember either.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, finished. I'm back now.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Okay. Donate, sell, or boxes?
